about.tagline: A lightweight web UI for the OpenRocket engine
about.body: {{name}} is a fast, mobile-friendly app for designing and simulating model rockets. It runs the real OpenRocket physics engine — compiled to WASM and JavaScript — entirely in your browser, so there's nothing to install and nothing leaves your device.
about.ork: Full OpenRocket (.ork) support: open, edit, and save your designs round-trip.
about.scope: It's a streamlined interface over the same trusted simulation core, focused on the essentials: live CG / CP / stability, 2D & 3D views, and flight simulation. If you need more of its capabilities, please refer to <orLink>OpenRocket</orLink>.
about.wip: ⚠️ Work in progress (pre-1.0) — features may be incomplete, change, or break.
about.credits: Physics by OpenRocket (GPL-3.0), compiled to WASM and JavaScript with TeaVM.
about.enginePin: Engine extracted from OpenRocket commit <commitLink>{{ref}}</commitLink>, dated {{date}}.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: {{name}} runs entirely in your browser. There are no accounts, no tracking, no analytics, and no ads.
privacy.storage: Your designs, simulations, preferences, and any custom materials or motors are saved in your browser's local storage, on your device — never sent to us or anyone else. Clearing your browser data (or using New) removes them.
privacy.network: The app downloads its motor and component catalogs from a public content-delivery network, and when you pick a motor it may fetch that motor's thrust-curve data from a public motor database; both are cached locally and subject to those providers' terms. Otherwise the app makes no network calls with your data.
privacy.hosting: Whoever hosts the app may keep standard web-server access logs (such as IP address and timestamp), as any website does. The app itself collects nothing.

settings.railExitMinHint: Below this the fins have too little airflow to steer, so the rocket can weathercock into the wind or go unstable as it leaves the rod.
settings.deploySpeedWarnHint: Single deployment (no drogue): above this speed, opening the parachute risks zippering the airframe or tearing the canopy.
settings.mainHighSpeedWarnHint: Dual deployment: above this the MAIN is coming out too fast — usually a drogue too small to slow the rocket, or a main set to deploy too high.
settings.mainLowSpeedWarnHint: Dual deployment: below this the main opens while the rocket is barely descending, which normally means it deployed near apogee — a slow, drifty descent from full altitude.
settings.drogueLowSpeedWarnHint: Dual deployment: below this the drogue comes out too slowly at apogee to inflate properly. Applies only to a stage carrying a chute or streamer marked as a drogue.

sim.safetyAckBody: Folding these away does not change what the simulation cannot tell you: fin flutter, structural loads, parachute inflation and opening shock, and how your motor performs on the day. You are still responsible for verifying the rocket on the bench and for flying under your safety code. The heading stays above the numbers, and the notes are one click away.

warnHelp.RECOVERY_HIGH_SPEED: The recovery device opened while the rocket was still moving fast. The shock loads the airframe and the canopy at once: it can zipper the body tube, tear the chute or pull the shroud lines out. Deploy nearer apogee, or fly dual-deployment with a drogue and a lower main.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_MAIN_HIGH_SPEED: On a dual-deployment flight the main should open slowly, already under drogue. This one opened fast enough to risk the same zippering and canopy damage — usually a drogue that is too small to slow the rocket, or a main set to deploy too high.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_MAIN_LOW_SPEED: The main opened while the rocket was barely descending, which normally means it deployed at or close to apogee. Nothing breaks, but the point of dual deployment is lost: the rocket floats down from full altitude and drifts a long way downwind.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_DROGUE_LOW_SPEED: The drogue opened while the rocket was barely moving, so it does little to stabilize the descent. Usually a drogue deployed well before apogee.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_LAUNCH_ROD: A recovery device deployed while the rocket was still on the rod. Check the ejection delay and the deployment settings — as simulated, the flight ends at the pad.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_DROGUE_NO_MAIN: A drogue deploys but no main follows, so the rocket descends the whole way on the drogue alone. That is a fast landing unless the drogue is sized to take it.
warnHelp.NO_RECOVERY_DEVICE: Nothing deploys, so the rocket falls ballistic and the landing speed below is what it hits the ground at.
warnHelp.LargeAOA: The rocket flew at an angle of attack outside the range the Barrowman method is valid for, so the aerodynamic numbers around that point are approximate. Common in strong wind or just after a slow rod exit.
warnHelp.LargeAOA.str1: The rocket flew at an angle of attack outside the range the Barrowman method is valid for, so the aerodynamic numbers around that point are approximate. Common in strong wind or just after a slow rod exit.
warnHelp.LargeAOA.str2: The rocket flew at an angle of attack outside the range the Barrowman method is valid for, so the aerodynamic numbers around that point are approximate. Common in strong wind or just after a slow rod exit.
warnHelp.SUPERSONIC: Part of the flight is supersonic, where the extended Barrowman method is an approximation. Treat the drag and stability figures through that region as indicative.
